title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering race during regional failover
author: Asha Patel
description: This hotfix addresses a race in the SLO enforcer backoff ordering logic that caused repeated regional failovers and load-shedding thrashing under bursty traffic. Root cause: concurrent backoff updates from regional controllers could reorder per-region backoff timers when requests raced during a failover window, causing the enforcer to oscillate between regions and over-shed capacity. Changes: 1) add monotonic sequence numbers to backoff updates so later updates can't be applied out-of-order; 2) switch per-region backoff store to compare-and-swap updates with a compare key (seq, timestamp) to ensure idempotent ordering; 3) add a short randomized jitter and hysteresis window to regional failover decisions to prevent tight loops; 4) increase default backoff cap from 30s to 60s and add rate-limited decay to avoid immediate recovery thrash; 5) add targeted unit and integration tests that reproduce the race and validate ordering guarantees; 6) export new metrics (slo_enforcer.backoff_applied_seq, slo_enforcer.failover_hysteresis_suppressed) and a dashboard note. The fix is implemented in services/slo-enforcer and includes a small config bump in configs/slo/defaults.yaml. This PR was tested locally and in a canary region with a synthetic traffic spike. Checklist: ensure small footprint on hot path, add tests, update dashboards, notify on-call. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan.
